rationale: Greek-derived compound, possibly παρα-ἀρχηγός 'one-alongside-the-founder' or παράγωγος 'leader, conductor.' Self-designation by Mani in autobiographical context: 'since I am the παραρχηγος, the fifty elect were with me, while I was head over the church.' The παρα- prefix may emphasize companion/secondary leadership under the cosmic Father, or simply derive from a hapax form. Cf. ⲛⲁⲣⲭⲏⲅⲟⲥ 'leaders/chiefs' in glossary.

Substantival use of ⲥⲁⲧⲡ̄/ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ ('chosen, elect') as 'a chosen item, a special matter' in the parallel ⲡⲙⲁϩϣⲁⲙⲧ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁⲧⲧ 'the third chosen matter' alongside ⲡⲙⲁϩⲥⲛⲉⲩ ⲛϩⲱⲃ 'the second matter.' The Lyc. -ⲧⲧ for -ⲧⲡ̄ is dialectal. Distinct from the proper-noun ⲡⲥⲁⲧⲧ as epithet of Zarathustra.
Indefinite noun in almsgiving-context: 'to give him some help to righteousness.' Possibly compound ⲟⲩ-ⲃⲁ-ⲟⲩⲁⲛ 'a-thing-of-any-kind.' Functions as a generalizing direct object for charitable giving.

Lycopolitan verbal stem 'give' with object suffixes: ⲧⲉⲉ-ⲥ 'give her,' ⲧⲉⲉ-ϩ 'give him,' ⲧⲉⲓ̈-ⲧⲟⲩ 'give them.' Recurring throughout this kephalaion (lines 3, 8, 9, 16, 18) as the principal verb of charitable giving. Distinct from the regular ⲧⲁⲩⲟ 'utter, send forth.'

Coptic numeral ⲡ̄ⲁ̄ (80+1=81) used in the manuscript as a chapter-numbering bracket-marker, appearing both before and after the chapter title. Distinguishes this kephalaion as Chapter 81 of the collection.

proposed_english: to bring them / to lead them
rationale: Lycopolitan infinitive ⲉ-ⲣ̄- + ⲁⲓ̈ⲧⲟⲩ ('bring/lead them,' related to ⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'bring' with 3pl object). Function: the brother is 'brought (to the church)' through the catechumen who has given gifts to righteousness. Pattern parallels ⲉϩⲁⲥⲱⲧⲉ 'to redeem' (line 7) — both are infinitive forms with ⲉϩⲁ- prefix.
